newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Wall Street rally seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Wall Street rally seen consolidating.

text.p: A rally in U.S. stocks has gained more credibility by spreading beyond big blue chip shares, but the market is now likely due for a near-term pullback to consolidate the advance, technical analysts said.
While some technicians see any fresh pullback as a pause in a new bull move on Wall Street, others remained cautious, saying stocks could be setting themselves up for a return to recent lows.

A fierce rally in U.S. stocks has shot the Dow industrials up 12.8 percent from their April 11 closing low at 6391.69 to Monday's record closing high at 7214.49. On Tuesday afternoon, the Dow was up another 52 points at 7266.

The first weeks of the rebound focused primarily on blue chips, raising eyebrows among technicians because of the rally's lack of breadth. But last week, broader indices encompassing smaller cap stocks began to participate.
The Nasdaq composite was up 11.5 through Monday from its recent closing low hit April 2 at 1201.00.
The Russell 2000 was up 7.9 from its recent closing low hit April 25 at 335.85.
"I think the seeds of a new bull leg have been sown in the bear market of the broad indices," said Elaine Yager, manager of technical analysis at Herzog, Heine, Geduld.
But she added, "I would like to see this very sharp advance pullback and consolidate to allow for this overbought condition to subside."

Some wary analysts noted that while the Dow industrials, the Standard & Poor's 500 and the Dow transports have hit record highs in the latest rally, the Nasdaq composite index and the Russell 2000 have not confirmed the rally, remaining below their peaks.
The Nasdaq composite closed at a peak of 1388.06 on January 22. The Russell 2000 peaked the same day at 370.75.
The Nasdaq composite was off about eight points at 1331 on Tuesday. The Russell 2000 was flat at 362.
